title: IonQ to Acquire Elisity for Up to $1.3 Billion to Integrate Zero Trust with Post-Quantum Cybersecurity - Quantum Computing Report
gist: IonQ (NYSE: IONQ) agreed to acquire Zero Trust cybersecurity firm Elisity in an all-stock deal valued at up to $1.3 billion, including up to $150 million in earnouts, to pair its post-quantum cryptography and QKD hardware with Elisity's policy framework. It continues IonQ's roll-up of infrastructure and networking assets after SkyWater, ID Quantique and Qubitekk.

insights.claim: IonQ signed a definitive agreement to buy Elisity, Inc. in an all-stock transaction valued at up to $1.3 billion, including up to $150 million in performance-contingent earnouts.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Stock-funded deal dilutes IONQ holders; earnout portion ties payout to Elisity performance.
insights.quote: entered into a definitive agreement to acquire Zero Trust cybersecurity firm Elisity, Inc. in an all-stock transaction valued at up to $1.3 billion
insights.locator: Quantum computing platform and foundry operator IonQ

insights.claim: The deal uses a collar of $33.07 to $49.61 per share, with the share count set by a 20-day VWAP before closing, and Elisity will operate as a subsidiary under CEO James Winebrenner, keeping its brand and management after the expected Q4 2026 closing.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: The collar bounds dilution risk from IONQ price moves before closing; watch the Q4 2026 close.

insights.claim: Elisity has 100+ global enterprise deployments, is doubling revenue year over year with zero customer churn, and plays in a $10+ billion microsegmentation sector.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Strong growth and retention metrics help justify the price, but they are as reported and not independently verified in the article.

insights.claim: Elisity's addressable market is tied to federal post-quantum cryptography mandates under U.S. Executive Orders, giving regulatory demand behind PQC migration spending.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Government mandates provide a demand driver for PQC security vendors independent of quantum computer progress.

insights.claim: IonQ plans to combine its hardware-level post-quantum cryptography and quantum key distribution technologies with Elisity's software-defined Zero Trust policy framework, extending Elisity's IdentityGraph engine with cryptographic inventory and risk data.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Moves IonQ toward recurring enterprise security software revenue beyond quantum hardware.
insights.quote: extend Elisity’s IdentityGraph engine with cryptographic inventory and risk data
insights.locator: The acquisition expands IonQ’s security roadmap

insights.claim: The combined offering aims to let enterprise and government clients manage 'harvest now, decrypt later' vulnerabilities while keeping least-privilege network access controls during multiyear PQC migrations.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: The HNDL threat is the sales hook for near-term PQC spending.
insights.locator: The acquisition expands IonQ’s security roadmap

insights.claim: The Elisity deal continues IonQ's strategy of acquiring foundational infrastructure and networking assets, following SkyWater Technology (semiconductor foundry), ID Quantique (QKD) and Qubitekk (quantum networking).
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: IonQ is building a vertically integrated quantum-plus-security stack through M&A; watch integration risk and cumulative dilution.
insights.quote: building upon its previous acquisitions of semiconductor foundry SkyWater Technology, QKD pioneer ID Quantique, and quantum networking provider Qubitekk
insights.locator: The deal follows IonQ’s broader strategy
